audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with their own whys[] text and with the packet chart.
audit.why: whys[0] says level 1 is 'a wash' but the row read Ziggs; whys[1] says your second turret out-trades his bomb but the row read Skill; whys[4] says the level-6 window is 'even' but the row read Ziggs; whys[6] says he out-stats the nest entirely but the row read Heimerdinger. Heimerdinger wins 54.08% over 98 games — a front-loaded lane that Ziggs reclaims at two items.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 4, 6 flipped to Skill, Heimerdinger, Skill, Ziggs in both layers as one atomic group.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly ordered: Lvl 2-3 nest, Lvl 4-5 grenade peak, 1st item poke war, Late artillery scaling. That matches the corrected chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere, and Short Fuse (P) — the auto-attack reset that actually opens his damage — was never mentioned. Packet also flags 'Bouncing Bombs' as a near-miss name.
audit.why: Kit: Bouncing Bomb (Q) 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s at 850 range; Satchel Charge (W) 20/18/16/14/12s, knocks both of you away and can hexplode a vulnerable turret; Hexplosive Minefield (E) 16s flat, slows and deals reduced damage on repeat detonations on the same target; Mega Inferno Bomb (R) 120/95/70s at 5000 range. Your own grenade is 11s flat and only a direct hit stuns.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns added to the cooldown block and the mid plan; Short Fuse named as the step-back tell; 'Bouncing Bombs' corrected to Bouncing Bomb.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge was called matchup-defining without ever saying how long it is down.
audit.why: 20s at rank 1 down to 12s maxed — the longest window in his kit and the only stretch where he cannot reposition off your turret line.
audit.corrected: 20s/12s written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.mid.

edits.before: Ziggs reclaims it: full-AP Bouncing Bombs one-shot your turrets and chunk your squishy yordle from artillery range, and his E minefield plus W-Satchel zone deny the siege your nest needs.
edits.after: Ziggs reclaims it: a full-AP Bouncing Bomb every 4s one-shots your turrets and chunks your squishy yordle from artillery range, and Hexplosive Minefield plus Satchel deny the siege your nest needs.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge: 20s at rank 1, 12s maxed — his knockback escape, so the moment he spends it you walk him down. - Bouncing Bomb: 6s falling to 4s, the poke you simply eat. - Hexplosive Minefield: 16s flat. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 — bait it out, then commit while he has no way to reposition.

edits.before: That is Ziggs's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Satchel knocks you off your own turret line — that displacement is his whole plan.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: A Bouncing Bomb every 4s clears a clumped nest — spread the buildings.

edits.before: Track Ziggs's Satchel Charge: His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. When it is down — Turret nest + E stun.
edits.after: Short Fuse is an auto reset — his wind-up, not the bomb, is your step-back cue; when Satchel is down, nest plus centre stun.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Satchel Charge: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If behind, farm safe and let your spikes re-open the lane.
edits.after: Trade around Satchel Charge, 20s at rank 1: while it is down run the full pattern, while it is up give nothing. If behind, farm safe until your spikes re-open the lane.

notes: The _missing feed claims Satchel Charge bypasses stacking resistances (percent health). Riot's own description says only 'deals magic damage to enemies, knocking them away' — no percent-health component — so per the kit rule I trusted the description and wrote nothing about resistances being invalidated. Recorded as a derived-flag misfire. Mercury's Treads is already correct in report[8].t against a slow-and-CC artillery mage.
